case_title: SHIV SHANKAR PRASAD SINGH v. THE STATE OF BIHAR
statutory_provisions: IPC s.409, s.477A r/w. s.120B; Prevention of Corruption Act s.5(2) r/w. s.5(1)(c) and (d)
trial_court_outcome: Convicted of the offences under Sections 409, 477A of IPC and 5(1)(c) and (d) of the Prevention of Corruption Act
high_court_outcome: Confirmed the conviction but reduced the sentence
offence_finally_established: Criminal breach of trust, falsification of accounts, conspiracy
neutral_facts: The prosecution case was that the accused conspired to misappropriate bags of fertilizers and made false entries in the records. An initial complaint was lodged alleging misappropriation of 540 bags of urea, but an investigation revealed that the entire 1040 bags of urea were misappropriated. The accused were responsible for falsifying records to show that the fertilizers were delivered to the FCI godown, despite no actual delivery. The prosecution presented documentary and oral evidence, including entries in registers and statements from witnesses, to prove the conspiracy and falsification of accounts. The trial court convicted the accused, and the High Court confirmed the conviction but reduced the sentence. The Supreme Court upheld the conviction, noting that the evidence proved the guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubt.
